correctness.rationale: For ordinary blue-only forcing, three white vertices in one bipartition class form a permanent obstruction because the other class can omit at most one edge to them. With two whites, a force into that class requires a matched white index. The two/two case is frozen precisely when the matched supports coincide; otherwise one force reduces to the two/one case. All remaining cases admit explicit force sequences. Counting permitted patterns yields the five coefficients; equal-support obstructions are \(t(m-t)(n-t)+\binom t2\). A separate direct color-change simulator checks all 407040 initial colourings across 130 parameter triples; finite checks support but do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: A sharp, complete infinite three-parameter enumeration for a natural perturbation of bicliques reveals a nontrivial cardinality-phase transition after exactly one and two disjoint deletions, stabilizing thereafter. The four-white obstruction and exceptional-pair subtraction give a reusable structural description, while the balanced crown specialization gives exact counts for every forcing-set cardinality, not merely a recomputation of the known complete-bipartite minimum.
